title: TAMMs: Change Understanding and Forecasting in Satellite Image Time Series with Temporal-Aware Multimodal Models
claim: Prior work handles understanding and generation in disjoint, single-shot pipelines; ours unifies them in a closed loop with mutual guidance.
layout: 2 stacked sections: four prior panels above, one unified framework below, dashed divider
description: The figure has two stacked sections split by a dashed horizontal line. The top gray section is titled 'Prior Work Limitations' and has four boxed panels in a 2x2 grid: (a) single image captioning, (b) single image generation, (c) temporal change description with a non-MLLM model, and (d) temporal image generation. Each panel is a small left-to-right flow of image icons, blue arrows, model boxes and speech bubbles, and ends with a red X and a short limitation such as 'Lacks Temporal Context'. The bottom light-blue section shows TAMMs as a closed-loop framework. A satellite image time series feeds a blue dashed 'Change Understanding' region with a Temporal-Aware MLLM and a 'Rich Change Description' bubble. An orange dashed 'Future Forecasting' region holds a Consistency-Aware Diffusion Model. An orange 'Temporal Guidance' arrow and a circular black arrow link the two regions, and the output is a forecast image.
caption: Our TAMMs framework unifies temporal change understanding and future forecasting, using a temporal-aware MLLM to guide a diffusion model in a synergistic process.
abstract: Temporal Change Description (TCD) and Future Satellite Image Forecasting (FSIF) are critical, yet historically disjointed tasks in Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) analysis. Both are fundamentally limited by the common challenge of modeling long-range temporal dynamics. To explore how to improve the performance of methods on both tasks simultaneously by enhancing long-range temporal understanding capabilities, we introduce **TAMMs**, the first unified framework designed to jointly perform TCD and FSIF within a single MLLM-diffusion architecture. TAMMs introduces two key innovations: Temporal Adaptation Modules (**TAM**) enhance frozen MLLM's ability to comprehend long-range dynamics, and Semantic-Fused Control Injection (**SFCI**) mechanism translates this change understanding into fine-grained generative control. This synergistic design makes the understanding from the TCD task to directly inform and improve the consistency of the FSIF task. Extensive experiments demonstrate TAMMs significantly outperforms state-of-the-art specialist baselines on both tasks. Our dataset can be found at https://huggingface.co/datasets/IceInPot/TAMMs .
